Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! Pathum Nissanka is accompanied by Nuwanidu Fernando in the middle. Matt Henry will start the proceedings.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, New Zealand have posted a competitive total on the board and will have to bowl really well to defend it. Sri Lanka knows that they have done the hard work with the ball and just has to back that up with the bat and they will take a 1-0 lead in the series. Will they be able to do it? Or will the Kiwis stop them? We will find out soon. Join us in a bit for the run chase.

Finn Allen is up for a quick chat. He says that with the base that they hadthey were expecting a lot more but looking at the wicket we are happy with this score. He adds that the track certainly has enough for the bowlers as the tracking is helping the seamers and we have a solid total on the board so the team feels they could defend it.

For Sri Lanka, Chamika Karunaratne was the best bowler as he scalped 4 wickets at an economy below 4 and was well helped by Lahiru and Kasun as they scalped a couple each and also Dilshan Madushanka and Dasun Shanaka who took a wicket each. Whenever a partnership looked like stepping up on the paddle, Lankan bowlers broke through it. Shanaka was fantastic with his bowling changes and field settings. The run chase would be really interesting as the pitch is helpful for the bowlers who will be consistent in grouping while the batters would love their time in the middle as well.

After being asked to bat first the Kiwis started sensationally with debutant Chad Bowes and Finn Allen taking the attack to the Sri Lankan bowlers. The introduction of Lahiru Kumara into the attack proved vital for Dasun Shanaka as he removed Chad Bowes in his very first over. Sri Lankan bowlers kept taking wickets on a regular basis and never let the Kiwis settle down. The batter did get a good start but couldn't capitalize and convert it into a big one. Finn Allen scored a half-century and debutant Rachin Ravindra was impressive as he fell just one short of his half-century.

Sri Lanka has done tremendously well to pull back things in their favor by picking up wickets at regular intervals. From 147/3 after the 26th over to restricting the Kiwis to a score of 274 runs the visitors have helped themselves massively in the first ODI game of this series.

Sri Lanka’s tour of New Zealand now shifts to the second phase with the hosts claiming a 2-0 whitewash in the Test series over the visiting islanders. Sri Lanka were in a good position to win the first match but a last-ball defeat took the winds out of their sails and they suffered an inning defeat in the second Test match. They have an excellent opportunity to reverse their fortunes in the three-match ODI series and with Super League points for the upcoming ICC Cricket World Cup up for grabs, this contest will have an extra bite to it. New Zealand have managed to secure automatic qualification for the mega event but Sri Lanka find themselves out of the top eight and will need to win this series convincingly to avoid the grind of playing the qualifying round. We focus our attention on the first ODI which will be played at Eden Park in Auckland before the caravan moves to Christchurch and the series finale will be played at Hamilton. Both teams come into this series on the back of 3-0 losses against India away from home and will want to get some winning momentum in their preparations for the World Cup. Before the India series, New Zealand were in good form in 50-over cricket but will be missing a few key players that have been released to participate in the Indian T20 League. With Kane Williamson, Tim Southee, Devon Conway, and Mitchell Santner traveling to India, Tom Latham has been appointed as the captain and he will have Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson, and Glenn Phillips at his disposal only for this game before they too leave for their franchise commitments. Michael Bracewell was initially included in the squad but will miss out as well and is replaced by Rachin Ravindra. Tom Blundell and Will Young have been called back into the squad with Chad Bowes and Ben Lister the two uncapped players given an opportunity on the international stage. Ben Lister will only join the team after the first ODI along with Mark Chapman and Henry Nicholls who will be providing cover for the departing players. Daryl Mitchell, Matt Henry, Blair Tickner, Henry Shipley, and Ish Sodhi retain their place in the squad. Sri Lanka will be led by Dasun Shanaka and he will want to take this series very seriously but will be without Avishka Fernando, Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Ashen Bandara, Nuwan Thushara, and Jeffrey Vandersay from the side that toured India. The visitors have brought back Angelo Mathews into the setup as they look to bring some experience into a side that recently suffered a morale-dropping defeat against Afghanistan. Despite the absentees, Sri Lanka have most of their regular white-ball players at their disposal with Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis, Nuwanidu Fernando, Dhananjaya de Silva, Charith Asalanka, Sadeera Samarawickrama, and Chamika Karunaratne all a part of the batting unit. Chamika Karunaratne's medium pace will also be useful in these conditions as he forms a part of a well-equipped pace bowling contingent comprising Kasun Rajitha, Dilshan Madushanka, Lahiru Kumara, Pramod Madushan, and Matheesha Pathirana who could make his ODI debut along with yet another uncapped player Sahan Arachchige. Wanindu Hasaranga, Mahesh Theekshana, and Dunith Wellalage provide the team with spin-bowling options but with overcast conditions throughout the day, the venue may suit the pace bowlers more. Which of these two teams will start the series with a win? We will find out soon.
